propositions.name: bodies_as_material_points
propositions.statement: The bodies the physicist studies can be described as material points separated from one another by intervals enormous in comparison with their dimensions.
propositions.quote: There also we should see material points, separated from one another by intervals, enormous in comparison with their dimensions, and describing orbits according to regular laws.

propositions.name: atoms_analog_of_stars
propositions.statement: Atoms are infinitesimal stars that attract or repel each other along the straight line which joins them.
propositions.quote: These infinitesimal stars are the atoms. Like the stars proper, they attract or repel each other, and this attraction or this repulsion, following the straight line which joins them, depends only on the distance.

propositions.name: straight_line_joins_atoms
propositions.statement: There is a straight line which joins any two atoms and along which their attraction or repulsion acts.
propositions.quote: and this attraction or this repulsion, following the straight line which joins them, depends only on the distance.

propositions.name: force_depends_only_on_distance
propositions.statement: The attraction or repulsion between two atoms depends only on the distance between them.
propositions.quote: this attraction or this repulsion, following the straight line which joins them, depends only on the distance.

propositions.name: exponent_change_yields_diversity
propositions.statement: The diversity of physical phenomena arises from a change of exponent in the distance-law of atomic force.
propositions.quote: in place of the exponent −2, we have probably a different exponent, and it is from this change of exponent that arises all the diversity of physical phenomena

propositions.name: atoms_describe_regular_orbits
propositions.statement: The atoms describe orbits according to regular laws.
propositions.quote: There also we should see material points, separated from one another by intervals, enormous in comparison with their dimensions, and describing orbits according to regular laws.

propositions.name: atoms_can_never_budge
propositions.statement: It is meaningful to say that atoms transmit heat one to another and yet never budge.
propositions.quote: in it are indeed atoms acting at a distance one upon the other; they mutually transmit heat, but they do not attract, they never budge.

propositions.name: law_is_differential_equation
propositions.statement: A physical law is a constant relation between the phenomenon of to-day and that of to-morrow, that is, a differential equation.
propositions.quote: For us a law is something quite different; it is a constant relation between the phenomenon of to-day and that of to-morrow; in a word, it is a differential equation.

propositions.name: shared_today_tomorrow_ordering
propositions.statement: The distinction between the phenomenon of to-day and that of to-morrow is definite in the same way for anyone applying the law.
propositions.quote: it is a constant relation between the phenomenon of to-day and that of to-morrow; in a word, it is a differential equation.

propositions.name: universe_is_machine
propositions.statement: The universe is also a machine, much more complicated than all those of industry.
propositions.quote: The universe is also a machine, much more complicated than all those of industry, of which almost all the parts are profoundly hidden from us

propositions.name: energy_conservation_universal
propositions.statement: The principle of the conservation of energy applies to the universe as it does to any machine.
propositions.quote: Well, in regard to the universe, the principle of the conservation of energy is able to render us the same service.

propositions.name: visible_wheels_speed_comparable
propositions.statement: The rotation of two visible wheels can be compared to determine that one turns ten times less quickly than the other.
propositions.quote: We easily ascertain that the final wheel turns ten times less quickly than the initial wheel, since these two wheels are visible

propositions.name: couple_ratio_from_speed_ratio
propositions.statement: A couple applied to one wheel is balanced by a couple ten times greater applied to the other when their speeds differ by ten.
propositions.quote: we are able thence to conclude that a couple applied to the one will be balanced by a couple ten times greater applied to the other.

propositions.name: compensation_cannot_fail
propositions.statement: In a machine, the compensation of forces in the interior can not fail to occur.
propositions.quote: For that there is no need to penetrate the mechanism of this equilibrium and to know how the forces compensate each other in the interior of the machine; it suffices to be assured that this compensation can not fail to occur.

propositions.name: visible_motion_constrains_hidden_mechanism
propositions.statement: Observing the motion of visible parts lets us draw conclusions which remain true whatever the invisible mechanism.
propositions.quote: in observing the motion of those that we can see, we are able, by the aid of this principle, to draw conclusions which remain true whatever may be the details of the invisible mechanism which animates them.

propositions.name: carnot_degradation_of_energy
propositions.statement: There is a principle of the degradation of energy, called Carnot's principle.
propositions.quote: Carnot's principle, or the principle of the degradation of energy.

propositions.name: equality_of_action_and_reaction
propositions.statement: Action and reaction are equal, as stated by Newton's principle.
propositions.quote: Newton's principle, or the principle of the equality of action and reaction.

propositions.name: relativity_of_physical_laws
propositions.statement: The laws of physical phenomena must be the same for a stationary observer as for an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation.
propositions.quote: the laws of physical phenomena must be the same for a stationary observer as for an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation

propositions.name: uniform_translation_undetectable
propositions.statement: We have not and can not have any means of discerning whether or not we are carried along in a uniform motion of translation.
propositions.quote: so that we have not and can not have any means of discerning whether or not we are carried along in such a motion.

propositions.name: stationary_and_carried_distinguishable
propositions.statement: The category of a stationary observer and the category of an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation are conceptually distinct conditions.
propositions.quote: The principle of relativity, according to which the laws of physical phenomena must be the same for a stationary observer as for an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation

propositions.name: laws_comparable_between_observers
propositions.statement: What counts as a law of physical phenomena is comparable between a stationary observer and an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation.
propositions.quote: the laws of physical phenomena must be the same for a stationary observer as for an observer carried along in a uniform motion of translation

propositions.name: conservation_of_mass
propositions.statement: There is a principle of the conservation of mass, called Lavoisier's principle.
propositions.quote: The principle of the conservation of mass, or Lavoisier's principle.

propositions.name: principle_of_least_action
propositions.statement: The law of least action stands among the general principles of physics.
propositions.quote: it involved both the conservation of energy and that of masses, and the equality of action and reaction, and the law of least action, which appeared, it is true, not as experimental truths, but as theorems

propositions.name: principles_sufficient_for_knowledge
propositions.statement: Application of these five or six general principles to the different physical phenomena is sufficient for our learning of them all that we could reasonably hope to know.
propositions.quote: The application of these five or six general principles to the different physical phenomena is sufficient for our learning of them all that we could reasonably hope to know of them.

propositions.name: ether_exists_as_medium
propositions.statement: There is a medium, the ether, whose molecules are disposed in some manner.
propositions.quote: We know nothing as to what the ether is, how its molecules are disposed, whether they attract or repel each other; but we know that this medium transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations

propositions.name: ether_transmits_two_perturbations
propositions.statement: The ether transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations.
propositions.quote: we know that this medium transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations

propositions.name: same_time_transmission_meaningful
propositions.statement: It is meaningful to say the ether transmits the optical and the electrical perturbations at the same time.
propositions.quote: but we know that this medium transmits at the same time the optical perturbations and the electrical perturbations; we know that this transmission must take place in conformity with the general principles of mechanics

propositions.name: transmission_conforms_to_mechanics
propositions.statement: The transmission through the ether must take place in conformity with the general principles of mechanics.
propositions.quote: we know that this transmission must take place in conformity with the general principles of mechanics, and that suffices us for the establishment of the equations of the electromagnetic field.

propositions.name: generalization_yields_certainty
propositions.statement: The general principles seem to derive from their very generality a high degree of certainty.
propositions.quote: These principles are results of experiments boldly generalized; but they seem to derive from their very generality a high degree of certainty.

propositions.name: verifications_end_doubt
propositions.statement: Verifications multiplying in the most varied and unexpected forms end by no longer leaving place for doubt.
propositions.quote: the more general they are, the more frequent are the opportunities to check them, and the verifications multiplying, taking the most varied, the most unexpected forms, end by no longer leaving place for doubt.

propositions.name: central_forces_contain_principles
propositions.statement: The hypothesis of central forces contained all the principles as necessary consequences.
propositions.quote: The hypothesis of central forces contained all the principles; it involved them as necessary consequences; it involved both the conservation of energy and that of masses, and the equality of action and reaction
